 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts

 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
% JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no master services matched primary='*#7-2*/control_path_subsystem_jtag_master.master' fallback=''; available masters: /devices/10AX115H1(.|E2|ES)|10AX115H2|..@1#3-6.2#DE5/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #0)/phy_0/master ; /devices/10AX115H1(.|E2|ES)|10AX115H2|..@1#3-6.2#DE5/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #1)/phy_1/master ; /devices/10AX115H1(.|E2|ES)|10AX115H2|..@1#3-6.2#DE5/(link)/JTAG/(70:34 v3 #0)/nios2_0 ; /devices/5AGT(FC7H3|MC7G3)|5AGXBA7D4|..@1#7-2/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #0)/phy_0/master ; /devices/5AGT(FC7H3|MC7G3)|5AGXBA7D4|..@1#7-2/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #1)/phy_1/master ; /devices/5AGT(FC7H3|MC7G3)|5AGXBA7D4|..@1#7-2/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #2)/phy_2/master ; /devices/5AGT(FC7H3|MC7G3)|5AGXBA7D4|..@1#7-2/(link)/JTAG/(70:34 v3 #0)/nios2_0}

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome to Intel's FPGA System Console

 This Tcl console provides access to the hardware modules instantiated in your
 FPGA. You can use System Console for all of the following purposes:

    * To start, stop, or step a Nios II processor
    * To read or write Avalon Memory-Mapped (Avalon-MM) slaves using special
     masters
    * To sample the SOPC system clock as well as system reset signal
    * To run JTAG loopback tests to analyze board noise problems
    * To shift arbitrary instruction register and data register values to
     instantiated system level debug (SLD) nodes

 In addition, the directory <QuartusII Dir>/sopc_builder/system_console/scripts
 contains Tcl files that provide miscellaneous utilities and examples of how to
 access the functionality provided. You can include those macros in your
 scripts by issuing Tcl source commands.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
% JTAG_PROBE master={/devices/5AGT(FC7H3|MC7G3)|5AGXBA7D4|..@1#7-2/(link)/JTAG/(110:132 v1 #0)/phy_0/master} status=PROBED uid=0x00000000
JTAG_RESULT status=ERROR code=2 msg={no responsive master matched the requested probe}
